findings.issue: Nothing refuses an activation on a machine that already carries an installation. ActivateAsync calls WriteKeyFile(...) — which overwrites keys/installation.key with PasswordWrap/RecoveryWrap/MachineWrap/AdminWrap of a brand-new random DbKey — BEFORE DbSession.Open(_paths, dbKey) discovers that the existing SQLCipher database will not open with that key. The activation then throws, W04 shows the generic «تعذّر التفعيل», and the working installation can no longer be signed into: LoginService reads only installation.key, and the previous file survives solely as an undocumented installation.key.bak that InstallationKeyFile.Save happens to leave behind. No guard exists at any layer: W02SetupFile/W03SetupCheck/W04Account have no LoginService.IsActivated redirect (unlike W05Login, which does have one), MainWindow.DefaultStartPath and Home.razor only choose the default route, and InstallationService.CreateAsync's own double-activation guard fires far too late — after the key file is already gone. Reachable today via --start-url=/first-run and by any future in-app link to the first-run route (which the re-apply-an-updated-setup-file flow will need).
findings.fix: At the top of ActivateAsync, before WriteKeyFile, refuse when File.Exists(_paths.InstallationKeyPath) || File.Exists(_paths.DbPath) — return a refusal W04 renders in Arabic rather than throwing — and add the same `if (!Login.IsActivated) ... else Nav.NavigateTo("/login", replace: true)` guard that W05Login.OnInitialized already has to the OnInitialized of W02SetupFile.razor, W03SetupCheck.razor and W04Account.razor.

findings.issue: The organisation key pinned at activation is never used again, and neither is the installed device id or export sequence. Inspect(string packagePassword) always calls SetupExpectations.FirstRun(StagingDirectory), which leaves PinnedOrgSigningPub, InstalledDeviceId and InstalledExportSeq null; the Inspect(string, SetupExpectations) overload is called only from tests (verified: grep for SetupExpectations across src/Wakeel.UI, src/Wakeel.Desktop, src/Wakeel.Core finds no product caller that supplies them, and Installation.OrgEd25519Pub is written by ActivationService and read back nowhere). Two of the five refusal states the spec requires W03 to show — «هذه الحزمة أُعدّت لجهاز آخر» and «هذه الحزمة أقدم من الحزمة المثبَّتة» — are therefore unreachable in the shipped product, and ARCHITECTURE.md §3's «أول تشغيل يثق بمفتاح الهيئة الوارد في الحزمة ثم يثبّته في installation ويرفض لاحقًا أي حزمة بمفتاح مختلف» is only half implemented: the pin is stored but never enforced.
findings.fix: Give SetupInspectionService an overload that, when an installation exists, loads the Installation row and the setup.export_seq setting and builds `new SetupExpectations { PinnedOrgSigningPub = installation.OrgEd25519Pub, InstalledDeviceId = installation.DeviceId.ToString(), InstalledExportSeq = long.Parse(settings[AccountSettingKeys.SetupExportSeq]), StagingDirectory = StagingDirectory }`, and have W02SetupFile.InspectAsync call that instead of the bare Inspect(password).

findings.issue: The clock status line the spec requires («حالة الساعة أسفل (ClockCheckService)») never reflects a check. `_clock` is initialised to ClockVerdict.Ok and the only assignment is inside RunClockCheckAsync, which runs after a successful sign-in and is immediately followed by Nav.NavigateTo("/w08"), so its result is never drawn on W05. The chip consequently always reads «ساعة الجهاز سليمة» with a green Success variant. Confirmed live: the host launched with --data-folder pointing at a folder whose wakeel.db is a 2-byte dummy still rendered «ساعة الجهاز سليمة • الأربعاء 16/09/2026 — 15:43». The screen states as fact something it has not verified (AGREEMENT item 20).
findings.fix: In OnInitialized, run a database-free pre-check from what W05 already has: set `_clock = ClockVerdict.Bad` when Time.GetUtcNow() < _options.BuildDate, or when _profile.LastSignInAt is set and Time.GetUtcNow() < _profile.LastSignInAt - ClockCheckService.BackwardTolerance (inject AccountOptions for the build date). Keep the ClockCheckService run after sign-in so the check is still recorded in clock_checks.

findings.issue: Only `CryptoException` with `ErrorCode.WrongPassword` is caught around the key-wrap opens, but KeyWraps.OpenWithPassword / OpenWithRecoveryCode also throw ErrorCode.Corrupt («The stored key is missing its derivation settings», «The stored key carries two different salts») and ErrorCode.UnknownKind (src/Wakeel.Crypto/Keys/KeyWrap.cs lines 148, 166, 171, 180). A damaged installation.key therefore escapes SignInAsync (and, identically, LockService.UnlockAsync and RecoveryService.Verify/RecoverAsync) as an unhandled exception. W05Login.SignInAsync, W06LockOverlay.UnlockAsync and W07RecoveryDialog.OnCodeChanged — the last of which calls Recovery.Verify synchronously from a Blazor event handler — have no catch of their own, so the screen dies instead of showing «تعذّر فتح بيانات هذه النسخة». This is exactly the «ملف تالف ... له رسالة وإجراء» case in the B1 acceptance criteria and the UserFacingError rule of ARCHITECTURE.md §10.
findings.fix: Widen each handler to `catch (CryptoException exception)` and branch inside: ErrorCode.WrongPassword keeps the current wrong-password result, every other code returns SignInOutcome.DatabaseUnreadable (Ar.FirstRun.Login.DatabaseUnreadable) in LoginService/LockService and RecoveryOutcome.KeysMissing in RecoveryService.Verify and RecoverAsync.

findings.issue: OnCodeChanged calls Verify(), which calls RecoveryService.Verify, which runs a full Argon2id derivation (the shipped parameters are 64 MB / 3 passes per ARCHITECTURE.md §3) synchronously on the render thread. The length guard only delays it until 21 characters are present; every further keystroke, backspace-and-retype, or paste re-runs it, freezing the window for roughly a second each time. Every other Argon2id call in this package (W02.InspectAsync, W04.StartAsync, W05.SignInAsync, W06.UnlockAsync, W07.SubmitAsync) is deliberately pushed off the UI thread with Task.Run; this one is the single exception.
findings.fix: Make Verify async: `_verifying = true; var outcome = await Task.Run(() => Recovery.Verify(code)); _verifying = false;` behind a busy flag so only one derivation runs at a time and only the latest text is verified (drop the result if _code changed meanwhile), and call the same async path from ScanAsync.

findings.issue: In StartAsync the `finally` block runs on the failure path too, so `Sheet = null` wipes the recovery sheet off the screen even when Activation.ActivateAsync threw and `_error = Ar.FirstRun.Account.ActivationFailed` is being shown. ActivationService still holds the same RecoverySheet and the same code, so a retry would activate with a code the person can no longer see or print — the opposite of the «تُعرض مرة واحدة فقط، اطبعها الآن» contract the screen just made.
findings.fix: Move `_password = null; _confirm = null; Sheet = null;` out of the `finally` and into the success path after the Task.Run returns (keep `_busy = false` in the finally), or set `Sheet = Activation.Sheet;` in the catch before returning.

findings.issue: When SignInProfileStore.Load() returns an empty profile — which happens by design whenever the DPAPI-sealed keys\session.dat cannot be opened (a ProgramData folder restored onto another machine, a rebuilt Windows profile, a deleted card) — W05 still renders the identity block from the empty values. Observed live on the host: «• الموظف رقم 0 • الجهاز 0» with a dangling leading bullet, an empty name line, and a footer «إصدار الوكيل v0.21 — الجهاز 0». SignInProfileStore's own XML doc promises the screen then «simply shows the product's own branding and asks for the password anyway», which only OrgName actually does.
findings.fix: Guard the identity block on `_profile.HasIdentity`: when false, omit the WAvatar/name/IdentityLine rows and the «لست أنت؟» button, and use Ar.FirstRun.Login.FooterLine's device number only when _profile.DeviceNo > 0.

findings.issue: UnlockAsync counts nothing. A wrong password on the W06 overlay returns SignInOutcome.WrongPassword without touching SignInProfile.FailedAttempts, UnloggedFailures or LockedUntil, and without writing an audit entry, so an unattended machine that locked itself allows unlimited password guessing while W05 stops after five. Argon2id throttles the rate but the counter and the temporary lock-out the product promises are simply absent on this path.
findings.fix: Extract LoginService.RecordFailure / LockedUntil bookkeeping into something LockService can call (or inject LoginService) and route UnlockAsync's WrongPassword branch through it, honouring an in-force lock-out at the top of UnlockAsync the way SignInAsync does.

findings.issue: In SignInAsync the two key-wrap opens sit in a try whose catch returns RecordFailure(...), while the zeroing finally belongs to the *next* try. If the password opens the DbKey wrap but the VaultKey wrap then throws WrongPassword (a key file written by two different passwords, i.e. a partially failed recovery), the already-derived plaintext DbKey is returned from the catch without CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory ever running on it. LockService.UnlockAsync has the same shape.
findings.fix: Declare the two arrays before the try and zero them in the catch before `return RecordFailure(profile, now);` (or fold both opens and the use into one try/finally that always zeroes).

findings.issue: The shared bUnit base class now calls `Services.AddWakeelCore()` with no options, so WakeelCoreOptions.Paths defaults to WakeelPaths.Default() — the operator's real C:\ProgramData\Wakeel — for every UI test that does not override it (FirstRunScreenContext does; ShellTests and the component tests do not). No current test writes there, but any future shell test that touches SignInProfileStore, LoginService.IsActivated or EnsureDirectories would read or write the machine's real installation folder.
findings.fix: Give WakeelTestContext its own per-test temporary root: `var root = Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "wakeel-ui-tests", Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")); Services.AddWakeelCore(o => o.Paths = WakeelPaths.ForRoot(root));` and delete it on dispose, as FirstRunScreenContext already does.

findings.issue: Ar.FirstRun.Login.CapsLockHint («مفتاح Caps Lock مفعّل — قد يكون سبب الخطأ.») is rendered in a bare `<span>` inside `.w05-caps`, with no <bdi>, no Bidi.Wrap and no unicode-bidi in W05Login.razor.css — the only mixed Arabic/Latin line in the package that is not isolated (item 55). It happens to render correctly today because both neighbours are spaces, but it is exactly the pattern the rule exists to prevent, and the same file isolates every other mixed line.
findings.fix: Render it as `<Bdi Text="@Ar.FirstRun.Login.CapsLockHint" />`, or isolate just the key name inside the constant the way Ar.FirstRun.SetupExtensionInline does (U+2066 … U+2069 around «Caps Lock»).

findings.issue: Ar.FirstRun.Setup.DiskFull («لا توجد مساحة كافية على القرص…») is declared but referenced nowhere (only FolderNotWritable is used, in W02). A full disk during W04's activation — the moment the key file, the database and four vault files are written — falls into W04's blanket `catch (Exception ...)` and shows the generic ActivationFailed. The B1 acceptance criteria name «قرص ممتلئ» explicitly as a state that must have its own message and action.
findings.fix: In W04Account.StartAsync catch IOException separately and test the HRESULT for ERROR_DISK_FULL/ERROR_HANDLE_DISK_FULL (0x27 / 0x70) to show Ar.FirstRun.Setup.DiskFull, and do the same in SetupInspectionService.StageAsync, which currently maps every IOException to CannotReadFile.

missing_spec_items: W03: the refusal states «حزمة لجهاز آخر» and «حزمة أقدم من المثبَّتة» are implemented in Wakeel.Crypto/Setup and covered by tests, but no product code path ever supplies InstalledDeviceId or InstalledExportSeq, so neither state can occur in the shipped application (see finding 2).
ARCHITECTURE.md §3: the organisation key is pinned into `installation` on activation but is never read back, so «يرفض لاحقًا أي حزمة بمفتاح مختلف» is not enforced anywhere in the product.
W05: the clock status line is not produced by ClockCheckService (or by any check) before sign-in; it is hard-coded to «ساعة الجهاز سليمة» (see finding 3).
Acceptance criteria: the «قرص ممتلئ» error state has no dedicated message or action — Ar.FirstRun.Setup.DiskFull is declared and unused.
W07: the optional new recovery sheet is shown with its code and QR but has no print / «حفظ PDF» action, so the person must copy 21 characters by hand; W04's sheet has both.

Drag-and-drop of a .wakeel-setup file onto the window (MainWindow.HandleDrop → SetupFileDrop → W02) compiles and is wired but has never been exercised at runtime (the builder's own open issue; a WPF drop cannot be synthesised through CDP). Not verifiable in this review either.
notes:
BUILD AND TESTS — ran exactly the prescribed command; full output read. `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Desktop` 0 warnings / 0 errors; `dotnet build tests/Wakeel.Walkthrough.Tests` 0 warnings / 0 errors; Walkthrough 11/11, Core.Tests 175/175, UI.Tests 201/201, all green, TreatWarningsAsErrors clean. Only ProjectReferences were added to the walkthrough csproj; no new NuGet package; no file outside the allowed paths changed (verified with git status).

HOST RUN (both branches, both hosts killed afterwards; ports 9361/9362 to avoid colliding with the other agent's 9333). Empty --data-folder → /json/list reports https://0.0.0.1/first-run; screenshotted W02 (dark): no sidebar, approved brand block, three-step rail with step 2 current, signed-package notice, drop zone doubling as picker, package-password field with reveal, «فحص الحزمة», «أين أجد الملف؟», dated footer — matches design/exports/preview/*/W/W02 (which I viewed light, and W03/W04/W06/W07 dark, W05 light). The folder came out with the full ARCHITECTURE §2 layout (data, vault, keys, models, packages, backups, logs, staging) and a clean one-line log. Second launch against a folder holding keys/installation.key + data/wakeel.db → /login, screenshotted W05: org fallback branding, avatar, password with show/hide, «دخول», «نسيت كلمة المرور؟ استخدم ورقة الاسترداد», clock chip, version/device footer. So the startup route decision is genuinely correct both ways. That same screenshot is the live evidence for findings 3 (clock chip green over a dummy database) and 7 («الموظف رقم 0 • الجهاز 0»).

BIDI — I did not take the builder's word on the extension token. Read the DOM over CDP: the text node carries U+2066 . w a k e e l - s e t u p U+2069 . and Range.getClientRects gives sentence-dot 712–715, isolate-dot 715–718, word 718–800, i.e. the dot sits with its word, correctly. Every other mixed line in W02–W07 goes through <Bdi>/<bdi>; the one exception is the Caps Lock hint (finding 11).

SECURITY, POSITIVE — ActivationService.WriteKeyFile creates exactly the four wraps of ARCHITECTURE §3 for both DbKey and VaultKey, each with kdf.WithFreshSalt(), plus AdminWrap sealed to the org X25519 key from the file; DbKey and VaultKey are 32 random bytes, handed to DbSession/AccountSession and zeroed in a finally; the device seeds move out of the staged payload into the key file sealed under DbKey. Staging is paths.StagingDir\setup (+\payload) — SetupPackageReader.Inspect throws when StagingDirectory is empty, so there is no %TEMP% fallback anywhere — and ClearStaging deletes it recursively after activation (asserted). The DPAPI protector zeroes both its own input copy and the OS's LocalAlloc'd output before LocalFree. The walkthrough sweeps every byte the installation wrote (db, key file, vault, sealed card, log) for both passwords, the package password and both recovery codes in UTF-8, UTF-16 and base64, and the log text as well — those are real assertions, not tautologies, and the same file's AssertArabicAndPlain rejects any Latin letter and the words خادم/منفذ/إنترنت in every message and audit summary. The lock-out doubles per round and is capped; a correct password is refused while a lock-out stands; recovery replaces the PasswordWrap so the old password stops working (asserted). LockService only consults the machine wrap after the password has opened its own wrap in the same session, as §3 requires.

DESIGN DEVIATIONS THAT ARE CORRECT — the W02/W03 previews show a 7-day package validity and a 16-character recovery code; ARCHITECTURE §3/§4 (decisions of 2026-09-15/16) replace both with «لا تاريخ انتهاء» and a 20+1-character Crockford code, and the implementation follows the architecture, not the picture. W03's check list is a superset of the preview's seven lines (it adds the guide, both templates and the revocation list), which the spec asks for. Ar.FirstRun's «يعمل الوكيل دون إنترنت» and the Caps Lock / Enter / QR / PDF / v0.21 tokens are all present in the approved previews.

ONE ARCHITECTURAL NOTE, NOT A FINDING — the MachineWrap is DPAPI at LocalMachine scope with a constant entropy string compiled into the assembly, so any local account on that computer can unwrap DbKey from installation.key; the same is true of the sealed sign-in card. That is precisely what ARCHITECTURE §3 specifies, and the policy statement «لا يكفي وحده لفتح البيانات» is enforced in LockService rather than by cryptography. The builder implemented the spec faithfully; it is the spec that should be revisited if the threat model includes other local accounts.

VERDICT — fix. Build and tests are green and the package is substantially complete and carefully built, but one high finding (an unguarded activation destroys the key file of an existing installation) and four mediums stand.
